title: Equal-Epoch Provider Deletion Conflict Adjudication

safety_properties.property: No adjudication preserves base fail-closed equal-epoch conflict behavior
Decision must choose an existing observation receipt for the exact logical job, object kind and observation epoch
Decision authority and rationale persist only as SHA-256 references
First durable decision for a conflict key is immutable; replacement is rejected
Decision sidecar is fsync plus atomic-replace durable and corruption fails closed
Chosen observation is revalidated against provider object hash, deletion timing and registry binding
Terminal erasure cannot be downgraded by adjudication
A newer applied or applying watermark makes an older equal-epoch adjudication stale
After restart, durable decision can resume and retire the pending equal-epoch conflict
Late same-epoch losing observations are ignored; equivalent chosen-state observations remain idempotently acceptable
Asset and task conflict keys remain independently scoped
Sidecar remains single-host evidence and does not claim distributed synchronization or product PARITY

isolated_interface_compatibility_harness.scope: new A37 logic against a contract-compatible in-memory base reconciler/registry stub

known_limits: A37 does not create provider truth; a human/HQ decision must still be backed by private authoritative evidence whose public durable representation is only a SHA-256 reference.
The base reconciliation ledger and A37 decision sidecar are single-host file-backed state. They are not a distributed transactional authority.
A37 does not establish provider deletion, account deletion, billing reversal, current-iPhone behavior or any PARITY row.
HQ/App must deliberately instantiate or integrate the conflict-resolving reconciler path; Shared/App composition is outside Worker 1 ownership.
A26 exact final-tip dependency/provenance audit remains separately pending on an executable full checkout or CI runner.
